html:
SMTO-KV-0003 — The agent used a note name SMTO can't accept

GUID: af6c0290-4afc-4750-a2b6-ac34b1decf1a
Slug: kv-invalid-key
Domain: KV · Subsystem: kv

What happened

  • Each note in the Task Scratchpad needs a short name. The name the agent used had spaces, symbols or other characters SMTO doesn't allow, or was too long, so the note wasn't saved or read.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Let the agent continue; it usually picks a valid note name and tries again. The rejected request didn't save or change any note.
  2. If you named the note yourself, use only letters, numbers, dots, dashes, underscores or colons, up to 160 characters, for example project-status. Names with spaces, accented letters or other symbols are refused.
  3. Don't rely on capital letters to tell notes apart; Status and status are the same note. SMTO stores note names in lowercase.

What success looks like

  • The agent saves or reads the note without this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep resending the same note name.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Agent KV key validation rejected a key that is not a string or does not match ^[A-Za-z0-9._:-]{1,160}$ (ASCII only; valid keys are lowercased).

What this means

  • Key normalization rejects a non-string or a value outside the ASCII key pattern before applying case normalization. KV checks apply only to the selected conversation. Rejected validation or compare-and-set does not authorize an unconditional replacement; diagnostics do not read or mutate additional stored values.

Why this can happen

  • Key normalization rejects a non-string or a value outside the ASCII key pattern before applying case normalization.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the key's exact shape and advertised 1–160 character bound; values follow a separate contract.

How to fix it

  • Use keys of 1–160 ASCII letters, digits, '.', '_', ':' or '-' (no spaces, slashes or non-ASCII characters); keys are case-insensitive. Correct the key in the kv__ call rather than retrying it unchanged.
  • Use an ASCII key containing letters, digits, dots, underscores, colons or hyphens within the advertised key limit.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The normalized key is accepted and addresses the intended conversation entry.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • KV checks apply only to the selected conversation. Rejected validation or compare-and-set does not authorize an unconditional replacement; diagnostics do not read or mutate additional stored values.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
